title: AI-Assisted Coders Run Windows on iPhone Duo, Build a Floppy Disk-Based AI Chatbot for MS-DOS - Slashdot

content_html:
The blog XDA Developers reports that a Claude enthusiast used the AI assistant to make a language model that runs off a floppy disk. "And you can stick it on a DOS computer to boot."

The language models "runs at a respectable speed, given that it's running off a CPU that was designed decades before LLMs were even a thing." Over on the ClaudeAI subreddit, user wollymonjak showed off this really impressive feat... [I]t's not going to be a particularly powerful AI; in fact, wollymonjak notes that if you ask something too complex or too long, it starts spitting out nonsense. But who cares about that when you're using a language model on DOS?
The same blog also notes that "the iPhone Duo hasn't been out for too long, and someone has already gotten Windows 11 on it." As spotted by TechSpot, this cool feat was performed by Ammaar Reshi over on X. Their project is called WindowsiOS, and its goal is to get Windows 11 running on an iPhone Duo without jailbreaking. Usually, when we cover a project coded up by AI, Claude is the one that called the shots; this time, Reshi opted to use Gemini 4 Carbon, Google's flagship model.
